title: Blue box transition and waste collection changes
subtitle: Recycling drop-off funding, curbside carts, downtown collection, Erb Street expropriation, Wilmot crosswalk, source water protection
overview: The committee spent most of the meeting on three waste management reports. The main decision was a recommendation that all contracts with Circular Materials end on December 31, 2025, and that continued recycling at the Cambridge and Waterloo drop-off sites, at about $300,000 a year, be considered in the 2026 budget {{vote:m6}}. Staff said producers used to fund half of that service and the funding ends January 1, 2026. They also said the figure may change after new provincial announcements.

Committee members also recommended asking the province to make producers responsible for recycling from sources such as public spaces, daycares and places of worship. The request also asks the province to explain its estimated $171M in municipal savings {{vote:m7}}.

Other recommendations supported source water protection policy amendments {{vote:m3}} and the expropriation of land for road improvements on Erb Street West {{vote:m4}}. A proposed pedestrian crossover in Wilmot was sent to Council for more information. The committee received reports on curbside carts, which start in March 2026, and on downtown collection. Downtown service stays unchanged on January 1, 2026.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended ending all Circular Materials contracts on December 31, 2025, and considering about $300,000 a year for recycling at the Cambridge and Waterloo drop-off sites in the 2026 budget {{vote:m6}}.

The committee recommended that Council ask the province to amend the Blue Box regulation so producers handle end-of-life recycling from all sources, and share the request with other municipalities and provincial officials {{vote:m7}}.
The committee added a request that the Minister of the Environment, Conservation and Parks explain the estimated $171M in municipal savings {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended expropriating part of a property at 658 Erb Street West, plus a temporary grading easement, for road improvements and a roundabout at Bourdeaux Place {{vote:m4}}.
The committee recommended supporting the draft water quantity policy amendments for the Guelph and Guelph/Eramosa wellhead protection area that apply in Waterloo Region {{vote:m3}}.
The proposed Level 2 Type D crossover at Huron and Milton streets was referred to the October 22 Council meeting, pending more information from staff.

debate: Several councillors questioned why the Region should pay about $300,000 for recycling drop-off when producers are now responsible. Staff said producers funded half of the service before, that the figure reflects new tender prices, and that it may change after talks with Circular Materials. A breakdown is promised for budget time.

Councillors asked for Circular Materials to appear before Council. Staff said they had asked and not yet heard back, and a staff meeting was scheduled. Some members called the changes confusing for residents, while another urged careful wording so the transition is not described as a disaster.

Councillors asked about practical curbside questions: when carts can be used, a second green bin, bags, and how yard waste and bulky items will be collected. Staff said carts should not be used until March 2026, only one green bin is offered for now, and yard waste stays manual.

On downtown collection, one councillor said collection moving to four days a week from seven was a major concern for businesses and cities, citing storage, trucks and winter start-up. Staff said four days was the level of service Council approved. They said they would keep working with business improvement areas and monitor results.

On the Wilmot crossover, a councillor asked why it lacked flashing lights. Staff said the Type D design gives pedestrians priority but has no lights, and agreed to report on the reasoning and the cost difference.
